info.name: Mini E-commerce REST API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the Mini E-commerce API.

This API has two kinds of account. A CUSTOMER shops; an ORGANIZATION user runs the shop. The collection logs in as both: {{token}} is the customer, {{org_token}} is the organization account. Requests that change the catalog, and everything under Organization, use {{org_token}}.

Setup
1. Start the backend: `python manage.py runserver`
2. Load sample data: `python manage.py seed_data --demo-user`
3. Import this collection and Mini-Ecommerce.postman_environment.json, then select the "Mini E-commerce - Local" environment (top right).
4. Run "Auth / Login" once. A test script stores the token in the `token` environment variable, so every protected request below works without copying anything by hand.

No request has a hardcoded id. Test scripts save ids into environment variables:
- `category_id` / `product_id`: the first item returned by the list endpoints
- `new_category_id` / `new_product_id`: objects this collection creates, which are the only ones the delete requests touch
- `order_id`: the order created by "Orders / Create order"

Because of that the whole collection can be executed top to bottom with the Collection Runner. "Auth / Logout" is deliberately last, since it invalidates the token.

Organization setup: create the staff account once with
    python manage.py create_org_user opsadmin --role admin
then run "Auth / Login (organization)".

request.description: Index of every endpoint. A good first request to confirm the server is up.

exec: // 201 on a new account, 400 if this username already exists.
console.log('Register returned ' + pm.response.code + ' - run Login instead.');

request.description: Create an account. Responds 201 with {token, user}. Passwords run through Django's validators, so a short or common password returns 400 listing exactly what is wrong. Running this a second time returns 400 (username taken) - use Login after that.

Exchange credentials for a token. The demo account comes from `python manage.py seed_data --demo-user`. A wrong password and an unknown username return the same 400 message on purpose, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover usernames.

Signs in an organization account and stores its token as `org_token`. Everything under Organization, and every request that changes the catalog, uses that token rather than the customer one.

Create this account first:
    python manage.py create_org_user opsadmin --role admin

The response's user.role will be "admin" and user.is_organization true.

exec: // Remembering who we are lets the Accounts requests avoid acting on
// the caller: an admin cannot change their own role or deactivate
// themselves, so those requests would fail for an uninteresting reason.

request.description: Returns the user the token belongs to. 401 without a valid token. The frontend calls this on startup to check a stored token is still good.
Public. Paginated, with product_count on each category. Supports ?search= and ?ordering=name or created_at.
Public. Uses the id saved by "List categories".

Requires a token; returns 401 without one. Category names are unique, so running this twice returns 400.

Requires an ORGANIZATION account: a customer's token returns 403. Run "Auth / Login (organization)" first.

Full update. Use PATCH with only the changed fields for a partial update.

Requires an ORGANIZATION account: a customer's token returns 403. Run "Auth / Login (organization)" first.

Deletes the category this collection created, so the seeded data stays intact. 204 on success, 409 if one of its products belongs to an existing order.

Requires an ORGANIZATION account: a customer's token returns 403. Run "Auth / Login (organization)" first.
Public, paginated 10 per page. The response has count, next, previous and results.
Case-insensitive match on name and description.
Filter by category id. ?category_name=phones filters by name instead.
?price=149.50 also works as an exact match.
Use -price for most expensive first. name, created_at and stock are also allowed.
page_size is capped at 100. Asking for a page past the end returns 404.
All query parameters can be combined; add &category={{category_id}} to narrow it further.
Uses the id saved by "List products".

The write field is category_id (a plain id), while responses return a nested category object. An unknown category_id or a negative price returns 400 naming the field.

Requires an ORGANIZATION account: a customer's token returns 403. Run "Auth / Login (organization)" first.

PATCH sends only the changed fields; PUT would require the whole object.

Requires an ORGANIZATION account: a customer's token returns 403. Run "Auth / Login (organization)" first.

Deletes the product this collection created. 204 on success, 409 if the product belongs to an existing order.

Requires an ORGANIZATION account: a customer's token returns 403. Run "Auth / Login (organization)" first.
Deliberately sends no Authorization header. Expected: 401. Reading is public, writing is not.

Deliberately uses the CUSTOMER token. Expected: 403. Reading the catalog is public, but changing it is an organization job - before roles existed, any registered customer could reprice or delete products.

Restock or correct a count. Send either a relative `delta` or an absolute `stock`, not both.

PATCH {"stock": N} also works, but writes back the number you last saw, so an order placed in between is overwritten. `delta` is applied to the row under the same lock the order path uses.

Only product_id and quantity are sent. The user comes from the token, and unit_price and total_price are calculated on the server - sending them has no effect. The product's stock is reduced by the quantity.
Expected: 400 with a message naming how many units are available. Stock is left untouched.
Deliberately sends no Authorization header. Expected: 401.
Only the token owner's orders, newest first, paginated.
Another user's order id returns 404, not 403, so order ids are not leaked.

item.name: Organization
item.description:
The API for the people who RUN the shop, mounted at /api/org/ and closed to customers: anonymous callers get 401, customers get 403.

Run "Auth / Login (organization)" first - these all use {{org_token}}, not the customer {{token}}.

Create the account it signs in as with:
    python manage.py create_org_user opsadmin --role admin

request.description: Every customer's orders, with the customer attached. The customer endpoint (/api/orders/) shows only your own; this is the opposite.
Anything not yet delivered or cancelled - the work queue.
Also ?status__in=pending,confirmed for several at once.
Or ?customer=<id>. Combine with ?placed_after= and ?min_total=.
Searches product name, username and email.
Every status and what may follow it. A client can build its buttons from this instead of hard-coding a copy of the rules that can drift from the server's.
Includes `events` (who changed what, when and why) and `next_statuses` (what the server will accept next).
Moves the order along. An invalid jump is refused with a message naming what is allowed instead, e.g. pending cannot become delivered.
Expected: 400, naming the transitions allowed from here.
Returns the ordered units to the product, exactly once. A reason is required. A shipped order cannot be cancelled - that would need a returns process.
Expected: 400. Blocking an order needs an explanation on record.
Deliberately uses the customer token. Expected: 403.

The state of the shop in one request: order counts, revenue, per-status breakdown, customers, catalog health, best sellers, what needs attention, and a daily trend.

Revenue is reported twice on purpose: `booked` is every non-cancelled order, `realised` is delivered only. Cancellations are excluded from both and shown separately.
days is 1-365 (default 30); low_stock_threshold defaults to 5.

With order_count, total_spent and last_order_at. total_spent excludes cancelled orders; order_count includes them - different questions.

Organization accounts are absent, so this endpoint cannot be used on a colleague or on yourself.
Best customers first. Also ?min_orders=, ?is_active=, ?joined_after=.
Their 10 most recent orders are attached.
Blocks sign-in and deletes their token, so the change ends the current session rather than only the next login. Their orders are left untouched. A reason is required.
Undoes a deactivation; they can sign in again.
Admin only. Staff may run the shop but not decide who else can - a staff token gets 403 here.

request.description:
PATCH also accepts role=customer, which revokes organization access while leaving the person able to shop. You cannot change your OWN role: an accidental self-demotion would end your access mid-session.

Acts on the colleague created above, never on yourself: an admin cannot change their own role.

Deletes their token too. You cannot deactivate yourself.

Acts on the colleague created above. You cannot deactivate your own account.
Undoes a revocation.
Deletes the token server side. 204 on success, and every later request with that token returns 401 - which is why this sits at the end of the collection. Run Login again to get a new token.
